purpose: Make EMBER-01 completion provable from the public repository. Before this pack the nine-leg completion receipt, the fresh green verification, and the launch-authority declaration existed only on the operator machine, so the completion claim rested on assertion rather than committed evidence (issue #1401).

artifacts.proves: All nine EMBER-01 certificate legs stood resolved-true simultaneously in one verifier run on 2026-08-02, with ok=true and an empty unresolved set. This is the receipt whose sha256 the freeze-lift record cites.

The nine legs still stand resolved-true at the current public tip, not only at the older 2026-08-02 tip. Its checkout block records head 363177c9, clean=true, and closure_sha256 e8287af1551d6115c4bd5355bab73f1b8452ca21ed6b31b6de25a0a10c4a09bc. This is the document the certificate binds as completion_receipt_sha256.

artifacts.redaction: worktree_path rewritten to the <USER_HOME> token per REDACTIONS.md. No other byte changed; the file still parses and every non-path value is byte-identical to the emitted receipt.
artifacts.proves: The 2026-08-04 verification was a real executed run, not a replayed record: job verify-msevylf8fjeaii, 2270014 ms wall, per-leg timings, detached worktree at the pinned commit, no reaped PIDs, ok=true.

The EMBER-01 certificate. SPINE_CERTIFIED was declared on the strength of the nine-leg completion (declaration_conjuncts.nine_leg_completion=true, birth_failure_classes_disposed=true, record_coherent=true), binding public_master_sha 363177c9, closure_sha256 e8287af1, and completion_receipt_sha256 752376cd — the verifier receipt in this pack. There is no separate EMBER-01 certificate file: this declaration is it.
The declaration was ledgered under certificate_sha256 10696f76, so the certificate above is the one that was actually declared rather than one produced afterwards.
The R1 WARM-100 run authorized by that certificate: run_id r1-warm100-20260804, seed 830001, 100 optimizer steps, and a requested_scope that sits inside the certificate's execution_scope.

artifacts.redaction: Project-drive paths rewritten to <TEMP_WORKSPACE> per REDACTIONS.md, keeping the repo-relative remainder. Four entries whose sources live in a private operator workspace outside this repository (input_authority, seat, subject_manifest, tokenizer) have their paths elided entirely; the sha256 in the certificate remains the binding for those.
artifacts.proves: Which source document each certificate sha256 was read from, so a reader can tell a repo-resident binding from a machine-bound one without guessing.

binding_sidecars_note: Five artifacts here cannot carry the repository's goal binding inline — their schema is fixed by the tool that emitted them, or their sha256 is cited elsewhere so no field may be added. Each binds instead through a content-addressed sidecar that names the artifact and records its digest, the same mechanism .github/labels.yml uses. The sidecars are plumbing, not evidence: they prove nothing about EMBER-01.

certificate_legs.5: reference model seat resolves and serves

claim_scope.note: Copied from the verifier receipt this pack ships: a bare clean clone honestly reports the operator-machine-bound legs (custody/identity/seat) as UNRESOLVED. ok=true requires an operator-machine run with real roots + owned checkpoint + seat.

reproducibility.basis: The split below is not asserted: it is what a verifier run off the operator machine actually returned. See receipts/ember-01-completion/live-census-verifier-replay-96d8c83-v1.json, which resolved legs 3, 4, 7 and 8 true and left 1, 2, 5, 6 and 9 unresolved.

reproducible_from_repository_bytes_alone.detail: Leg 7 re-runs tools/ember-restart-3b/launch_packet.py and leg 8 re-runs the authority conservation certificate; both read only tracked files.

machine_independent_given_custody_only_c.detail: Legs 3 and 4 re-derive and then tamper the owned checkpoint identity. The logic is machine-independent, but the checkpoint bytes are custody-only and are not public, so a stranger cannot supply the input. The public trace of leg 4 is receipts/ember-01-completion/cond4-tamper-battery-bf20f050-v1.json.

operator_machine_bound.detail: Legs 1, 2, 6 and 9 need the operator machine's 24 custody roots, which the census cannot bind on a bare clone; leg 5 needs the reference model seat with its runtime dependencies installed. On a stranger clone these legs return UNRESOLVED, never false — the verifier does not silently convert an absent binding into a passing one.

verification_procedure: sha256 every path in artifacts[] and compare against the recorded digest; all seven must match.

sha256 receipts/ember-02-launch-authority/certificate.json and confirm it equals the certificate_sha256 in declaration-ledger.jsonl and run-spec.json (10696f763a682e47e243d3b72cf6e85e24b128faeda43b69ee494e7438fcd8a0).
sha256 the verifier receipt in this pack and confirm it equals the certificate's completion_receipt_sha256 (752376cd1e67e966783b00975fa11916de7c424a8d98f094199aa44ed903da52).
confirm the certificate's public_master_sha equals the verifier receipt's checkout.head (363177c981fb7543dabb77d890c1652aa455dc51), and that both closure_sha256 values agree.
confirm every leg in the two nine-leg receipts reads resolved-true and that leg_summary.unresolved is empty.
re-run legs 7 and 8 from a fresh clone; expect them to resolve true. Legs 1, 2, 5, 6 and 9 will report UNRESOLVED off the operator machine, which is the honest result, not a failure.
frozen_bytes_note: Five artifacts here carry a sha256 that another document cites, so they are committed verbatim and are enumerated in tools/frozen-receipt-exceptions.json rather than being edited to satisfy the receipt schema floor. Editing a hash-cited document to please a checker would break the citation that makes it evidence.
